text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed little changed after holding to narrow ranges. March finished $0.80 higher at $299.60 per tonne, while May was up $0.10 at $298.20 per tonne. In New York raw sugar futures settled barely firmer in quiet dealings. March added 2 points to close at 10.44 cents/lb, while May was up 1 point at 10.39 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 1 and 3 points. There was no fresh news to give the market direction.

VENEZUELA - According to industry sources sugar production in 1996/97 is expected to reach 520,000 tonnes, white value, slightly down on last year's figure of 552,000 tonnes. Molasses production in 1996/97 is expected to reach 324,000 tonnes.

GERMANY - Sugar production in November 1996 amounted to 1.676 million tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 1.601 million tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/November) up to 3.682 million tonnes, up from last year's 3.284 million tonnes. Total production in 1995/96 reached 4.158 million tonnes against 3.991 million tonnes in 1994/95. Total production in 1996/97 is expected to reach 4.554 million tonnes. Sugar consumption in November 1996 amounted to 253,686 tonnes, down from last year's 262,125 tonnes. THAILAND - Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 27,448 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 32,939 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in November/December 1996 up to 55,578 tonnes against 75,444 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached the record high of 4.653 million tonnes compared to 3.847 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in November/December 1996 were Indonesia with 20,300 tonnes whites against nil, Cambodia with 6,270 tonnes compared to 3,811 tonnes and Malaysia with 5,000 tonnes raws against nil.

BRAZIL - Sugar production up to January 16 amounted to 13.673 million tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 12.875 million tonnes, official figures show. Total production in the Center South amounted to 11.310 million tonnes compared to 10.176 million tonnes, while output in the north-northeast reached 2.362 million tonnes, down from 2.698 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Alcohol production up to January 16 was 13.720 billion litres compared to 12.182 billion litres in 1995/96. Iran bought at least two cargoes of raw sugar and probably one cargo of white sugar, trade sources said. Iran's GTC (Government Trading Corporation) paid between $257 and $258 a tonne for two 15,000 tonne cargoes of raws, likely to be of Cuban origin, for March 15/April 15 shipment. Details on the white purchase were more sketchy but traders said they believe Iran bought 14,000 tonnes of March shipment at around $302 per tonne.
